thread:
Alex K.: hey folks, noticed a perf regression after the quant kernel-picker change rolled last night on h100s-sm104.
Ria S.: which model / seq len / quant mode?
Alex K.: llama3-8k int4 path. single-request seqlen bumped from 1k->2k in our canary, p95 latency +28%, throughput -22% at batch=4.
Samir P.: did kernel-picker switch to the new fused-int4 tile? could be memory-bank smearing or kvcache churn.
Alex K.: attaching quick perf snippet from the canary host:
```
2026-03-17 23:11:04 PID 2345 model=llama3-8k quant=int4 pick=int4_fused_sm104
p50=56ms p95=312ms tokens/s=18.4 memcpy=13.1ms stall=29.4ms
2026-03-17 23:12:04 PID 2345 model=llama3-8k quant=int8 pick=int8_fallback_sm88
p50=46ms p95=243ms tokens/s=23.5 memcpy=4.2ms stall=9.7ms
```
Alex K.: looks like the picker favoured the fused int4 kernel which is faster usually but under these seq/batch patterns we see memcpy & stall spikes.
InfraBot: deploy: kernel-picker v3 rolled to cluster-7 @2026-03-18T00:05Z (autorollback enabled)
Jules M.: two hypotheses: (1) fused-int4 increases per-layer temp buffers causing PCIe memcpy at certain seq/batch, (2) kvcache slot collisions due to different chunking.
Marina L.: can we reproduce locally with a seeded path of requests? maybe pathfinder_probe to capture ordering effects.
Samir P.: propose a lightweight tuning param: `seqlen_penalty_per_arch` + `kv_slot_throttle`. add a jittered probe sequence to avoid synchronized warmups across requests.
Alex K.: sample config I'm going to try in the probe:
```
{
  "kernel_picker": "pathfinder",
  "per_arch": {
    "sm104": {"seqlen_penalty": 0.18, "cold_bias": 0.06},
    "sm88":  {"seqlen_penalty": 0.08, "cold_bias": 0.03}
  },
  "kv": {"slot_throttle": 0.7, "warmup_window_ms": 120}
}
```
Ria S.: small ask: include the exact request sequence used in the canary so we can replay (same batch timings).
Alex K.: pasted the request generator params: `--model llama3-8k --quant int4 --seq 1024,2048 --batch 4 --interarrival 120ms --seed 1729`
Samir P.: also adding `smear_cohort_seed` to the probe to randomize which kernels get fried first. smells like synchronized cache-ejects.
Jules M.: if this config helps, we should add a per-arch "overflow_fallback_threshold" so picker falls back to int8 when memcpy > X ms.
Alex K.: running pathfinder_probe now, will post results in ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(30m later)

Alex K.: results summary from pathfinder_probe run-2026-03-18:
```
baseline (picker v3): p95=312ms tokens/s=18.4 memcpy=13.1ms stall=29.4ms
probe w/ seqlen_penalty=0.18 + kv_throttle: p95=245ms tokens/s=21.8 memcpy=6.0ms stall=12.1ms
probe w/ fallback_threshold=9ms: p95=230ms tokens/s=23.1 memcpy=3.9ms stall=9.3ms
```
Alex K.: tl;dr: small per-arch seqlen_penalty + kv throttle + memcpy threshold gets us back to prior perf and avoids int4 meltdown path. planning to push a conservative picker rule and more benching across sm95/sm104.
Marina L.: nice! can you add results to perf-dashboard and mark the canary for a slow ramp? I'll coordinate SRE on rollback window.
Samir P.: follow-up: add a telemetry tag for "probe_smear" so we can correlate incidents with cohort spikes.
Alex K.: will open a follow-up PR with config + telemetry. thanks all :thumbsup:
